body:
Calling out to `sh` once per prompt redraw is super expensive, performance-wise.
Why do this manually on windows but shell out on *nix?

> Calling out to `sh` once per prompt redraw is super expensive, performance-wise.
> Why do this manually on windows but shell out on *nix?

In my opinion, Starship does a lot of really expensive stuff on every redraw (for example, calling go binary or examining git status). An extra `sh` call is not expensive at all in comparison. On the upside, it's very simple.

But I can rework it for sure if that's the consensus.
It is not as expensive as, say, examining git status for a big repo, but it gets called indiscriminately on each directory, that's why I'm more worried about it than otherwise
Well, I do agree. I'll fix this, thanks

I think this test needs to be `#[ignore]`d, as it assumes the existence of `/etc`. [This is not a valid assumption on Termux](https://wiki.termux.com/wiki/Differences_from_Linux) which is a platform we support.

This looks great! I wouldn't mind a doc comment just generally explaining what this function is looking for (e.g. checks permission bits against current user's effective uid + list of groups) but otherwise I think it's ready to merge.

Alright, we're about to enter the area of the code I know nothing about, so forgive me if I sound like a total rube here. I just want to understand things well enough to where I could (at least try to) modify this if I need to in the future.

First, what is the difference between `GetFileSecurityA` (which I can find documentation for) and `GetFileSecurityW`?

Second, am I correct in saying that this call is only getting information about `length` so that we can allocate a buffer of the correct size?

Finally (and perhaps the gaps in my knowledge of `unsafe` are showing here), is there an implicit coercion that occurs from `&mut` to `*mut`? The crate docs say that you need an `LPDWORD` (i.e. `*mut DWORD`) for the last argument.

Clearly, we need to create an impersonation token here, but I'm having trouble understanding why. Is this because `AccessCheck` is a much more powerful API than just checking for file permissions, and so needs an impersonation token for other uses of it? Is this something that you just have to do when you want to call `AccessCheck`?

Of course, looking further down I see that our integration tests directly assume the existence of `/etc`...which I also think is in error, but now I'm not as sure. Regardless, let's `#[ignore]` this test to be on the safe side--it'll still run in the GitHub Actions CI environment, just not on systems where people download/build/test manually.

A suffix = ANSI string, W suffix = Unicode String
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/learnwin32/working-with-strings

AccessCheck requires an impersonation token (per https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/securitybaseapi/nf-securitybaseapi-accesscheck).
You can find some sample code on how to do call DuplicateToken here: 
https://github.com/jeanga/wil-rs/blob/abc43b2d3ec45896ebf2f3d19b380e7bfed085e6/src/token.rs#L139

HTH
The second question: yes, one can use type coercion to get a raw pointer from a reference in Rust. More info here: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.pointer.html
